business_model.claim: The company is a hotel REIT that owns urban and resort lifestyle hotels. Per its Q3 2026 release it owns 42 hotels with about 10,800 guest rooms across 14 markets, and it earns money from running those hotels.
quotes: The Company owns 42 hotels and resorts, totaling approximately 10,800 guest rooms across 14 urban and resort markets.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: The target is upper-upscale full-service hotels, branded and independent, in major gateway and leisure markets. The stated customer groups are business transient, leisure transient, and group and convention demand.
quotes: We focus on both branded and independent full-service "upper-upscale" hotels.
including business transient, leisure transient and group and convention room-night demand

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and risk factor sections.
business_model.claim: The company does not operate its hotels. To keep REIT status it leases them to taxable REIT subsidiary lessees, which hire third-party managers. The company's role is owner and asset manager.
quotes: which in turn engage third-party eligible independent contractors to manage the hotels

business_model.basis: Stated in the income statement; the share is my reading of the table and is not printed there.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from three lines: rooms, food and beverage, and other operating. For the nine months to September 2026, total revenues were 1,155,543 (table in thousands), made up of rooms 732,491, food and beverage 289,969 and other operating 133,083.

Revenue is driven by occupancy, average daily rate (ADR) and RevPAR. In Q3 2026 same-property occupancy was 80.6% against 79.6%, and ADR was $318.52 against $297.56. Management said these metrics depend on macroeconomic factors and on regional and local economies and events.
quotes: ADR, occupancy and RevPAR may be impacted by macroeconomic factors as well as regional and local economies and events.

business_model.basis: Stated in the release; the fixed-cost mechanism is partly from the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: The Q3 2026 release shows strong operating leverage. Same-property revenue rose faster than same-property expenses, and management says rate-led growth and cost efficiency are lifting margins.
quotes: Same-Property Total Revenue +6.9% versus expense growth of just 4.0%, driving 58% EBITDA flow-through and 205 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

business_model.claim: Operating costs fall into several lines. For the nine months to September 2026, the income statement shows hotel operating expenses of 741,344, depreciation and amortization of 155,795, real estate and property taxes, insurance and ground rent of 97,220, and interest expense of 78,319, all in a table in thousands.
The 10-K names the main hotel cost pressures as wages and benefits, repair and maintenance, property taxes and insurance.
quotes: wage and benefit costs, which may include an increase in minimum wages and health benefit costs; repair and maintenance expenses; property taxes; insurance costs; and other operating expenses

business_model.claim: Seasonality: the company says it earns less in the first and fourth quarters and more in the second and third. Q3 is therefore a seasonally strong quarter.
quotes: Generally, our hotels have lower revenue, operating income and cash flow in the first and fourth quarters of each year and higher revenue, operating income and cash flow in the second and third quarters of each year.

business_model.basis: Strategy is stated in the 10-K; the 2026 sales and impairment are stated in the 10-Q and its income statement.
business_model.claim: The company recycles capital by selling hotels and using the proceeds for debt reduction and share repurchases. In 2026 it sold the Chamberlain West Hollywood Hotel for $43.5 million and The Hotel Zags for $10.0 million, and in Q3 it recorded a non-cash impairment charge of 77,329 (table in thousands).
quotes: we may seek to sell hotels opportunistically if we believe sales proceeds may be used to repay debt, repurchase our shares or invest in other hotel properties that offer more attractive risk-adjusted returns

quotes: Net debt-to-trailing 12-month corporate EBITDA declined to 5.1x as of September 30, 2026, from 5.9x at December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: The company also holds a majority of the equity in Curator, a collection of small brands and independent lifestyle hotels and resorts. Curator is consolidated.
